newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but off peaks.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but off peaks.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended firmer on Friday, but off their highs following selected buying of blue chip counters on the cash market, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract finished five points higher at 18,135 after hitting a high of 18,440.
Dealers said the contract's ability to hold above the 18,000 level sent a positive signal but gains were likely to be slow.
"People are trading on the broad view that perhaps the worst of the storm is over and the market's found a base between 17,800 and 17,900," said a trader with a European house.
But he said the upside looked limited because there had been no outright fresh buying, only bottom-picking by bargain hunters.
"It broke through the 18,300 level today and that's good. The next target should be 18,545-18,575," said a trader with a local futures house.
But he said the March Nikkei was likely to encounter some profit-taking pressure on any rises to that region as its next technical target was about 200 points higher.
The March contract of the MSCI Taiwan index settled at its opening level after hitting a high of 311.5. Volume was 375 lots.
Dealers said the Taiwan stock market's breach of a six-year resistance level of 7,200 points on Thursday gave an early boost to the futures market.
